title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to electromagnetic compatibility (version 7.2.0, 07 series of amendments)
scope_summary: UN R10 approves vehicle types and electrical/electronic sub-assemblies (ESAs), as components or separate technical units, with regard to electromagnetic compatibility. It covers radiated and conducted emissions, immunity of safety- and statutory-relevant functions, and additional requirements for REESS charging coupled to the power grid, for vehicles of categories L, M, N, O, T, R and S and the ESAs intended for them.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to: 1.1 Vehicles of categories L, M, N O, T, R and S with regard to electromagnetic compatibility; 1.2 Components and separate technical units intended to be fitted in these vehicles with the limitation given in paragraph 3.2.1. with regard to electromagnetic compatibility.
applies_to_components: Electrical/electronic sub-assemblies (ESA) approved as component or separate technical unit (STU)
Electrical/electronic systems forming part of a vehicle
Vehicle wiring harness (supply, bus e.g. CAN, signal, active antenna cables)
Coupling system for charging the REESS (on-board/external chargers, charging interfaces: L1/L2/L3/N/PE/control pilot)

ESAs involved in immunity related functions (engine, gear, brake, suspension, active steering, speed limitation, seat/steering wheel positioning, dipped beam, wipers, indirect vision, blind spot, airbags/restraints, emergency calling, direction indicators, stop lamps, end outline/rear position lamps, emergency light bars, warning indicators/displays, anti-theft alarm, horn, data bus, tachograph, odometer, charging control)
Intentional RF transmitters fitted to vehicles
ESAs that are (part of) a light source
Aftermarket electrical/electronic equipment for motor vehicles
Signal/control ports and wired network ports of vehicles/ESAs in charging mode
AVAS (per UN R138) and AECS (per UN R144)
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3)

ESA that is (part of) a light source must cite an approval number under UN R37, R99 or R128, or provide a Technical Service report that it is not mechanically interchangeable with such light sources; otherwise R10 approval shall not be granted (paras 3.2.10, 4.2.4)
AVAS defined by reference to the latest series of amendments of UN R138
AECS defined by reference to the latest series of amendments of UN R144
ADS/DDT definitions based on ECE/TRANS/WP.29/2022/58 Annex 1; ADS driver responsibility may be specified in other UN Regulations
Note: immunity levels address one of the external environments for functional safety (e.g. ISO 26262)
Transitional provisions for 05 and 07 series of amendments (para 13)

defined_terms.label: Electromagnetic compatibility
defined_terms.definition: Ability of a vehicle, component(s) or separate technical unit(s) to function satisfactorily in its electromagnetic environment without introducing intolerable electromagnetic disturbances to anything in that environment.

defined_terms.label: Electromagnetic disturbance
defined_terms.definition: Any electromagnetic phenomenon which may degrade the performance of a vehicle, component, STU or any other device or system operated in the vicinity of a vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Electromagnetic immunity
defined_terms.definition: Ability of a vehicle, component(s) or STU(s) to operate without degradation of performance in the presence of specified electromagnetic disturbances, including wanted RF signals from transmitters or ISM in-band emissions.

defined_terms.label: Broadband emission
defined_terms.definition: An emission with a bandwidth greater than that of a particular measuring apparatus or receiver (CISPR 25).

defined_terms.label: Narrowband emission
defined_terms.definition: An emission with a bandwidth less than that of a particular measuring apparatus or receiver (CISPR 25).

defined_terms.label: Electrical/electronic system
defined_terms.definition: Electrical and/or electronic device(s) or set(s) of devices with associated connections forming part of a vehicle but not intended to be type approved separately from the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA)
defined_terms.definition: An electrical and/or electronic device or set(s) of devices intended to be part of a vehicle, with associated connections and wiring, performing one or more specialized functions, approvable as a component or a separate technical unit (STU).

defined_terms.label: Vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing essentially in engine compartment size/shape, general arrangement of electrical/electronic components and wiring, and primary body material.

defined_terms.label: ESA type
defined_terms.definition: ESAs not differing in the function performed and the general arrangement of electrical/electronic components.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle wiring harness
defined_terms.definition: Supply voltage, bus system (e.g. CAN), signal or active antenna cables installed by the vehicle manufacturer.

defined_terms.label: Immunity related functions
defined_terms.definition: Non-exhaustive list of functions related to direct vehicle control, occupant/road user protection, driver/road-user confusion (optical/acoustical), data bus functionality, statutory data, and charging mode when coupled to the grid.

defined_terms.label: REESS
defined_terms.definition: Rechargeable energy storage system that provides electric energy for electric propulsion of the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Coupling system for charging the REESS
defined_terms.definition: The electrical circuit installed in the vehicle used for charging the REESS.

defined_terms.label: REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid
defined_terms.definition: The normal charging operation mode of the vehicle and/or charging system.

defined_terms.label: Mode 1 charging mode
defined_terms.definition: IEC 61851-1 charging with the vehicle connected directly to AC mains without communication or supplementary pilot/auxiliary contacts.

defined_terms.label: Mode 2 charging mode
defined_terms.definition: IEC 61851-1 AC charging via a charging harness with an EVSE box providing control pilot signalling and shock protection, without communication with the mains.

defined_terms.label: Mode 3 charging mode
defined_terms.definition: IEC 61851-1 AC charging from an EVSE (e.g. charging station, wallbox) with communication between vehicle and charging station.

defined_terms.label: Mode 4 charging mode
defined_terms.definition: IEC 61851-1 DC charging from an EVSE with off-board charger and communication between vehicle and charging station.

defined_terms.label: Signal/control port
defined_terms.definition: Port for interconnecting ESA components or an ESA with auxiliary equipment (e.g. RS-232, USB, HDMI), including Control Pilot, PLC on Control Pilot and CAN for vehicles in charging mode.

defined_terms.label: Wired network port
defined_terms.definition: Port for voice, data and signalling connection to single- or multi-user communication networks (e.g. CATV, PSTN, ISDN, xDSL, LAN).

defined_terms.label: Asymmetric artificial network (AAN)
defined_terms.definition: Network used to measure or inject common-mode voltages on signal/communication lines of the vehicle in charging mode while rejecting the differential signal.

defined_terms.label: DC-charging artificial network (DC-charging-AN)
defined_terms.definition: Network inserted in the HV DC lead of a vehicle in charging mode providing a specified load impedance and isolation from the DC charging station.

defined_terms.label: Artificial mains network (AMN)
defined_terms.definition: Network (V-AMN/LISN or delta) inserted in the power mains providing defined RF impedance, coupling disturbance voltage to the receiver and isolating from the mains.

defined_terms.label: Automated Driving System (ADS)
defined_terms.definition: Vehicle hardware and software collectively capable of performing the entire Dynamic Driving Task on a sustained basis.

defined_terms.label: Dynamic Driving Task (DDT)
defined_terms.definition: The real-time operational and tactical functions required to operate the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Failure situations
defined_terms.definition: Situations where the ADS or another vehicle system has a fault that removes or reduces the ADS's ability to perform the DDT.

defined_terms.label: Residential environment
defined_terms.definition: Per IEC 61000-6-3:2020, locations for domestic dwellings directly connected to the low-voltage public mains network.

defined_terms.label: Non-residential environment
defined_terms.definition: Per IEC 61000-6-4:2018, locations with a separate power network supplied from a high- or medium-voltage transformer (industrial locations).

defined_terms.label: Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System (AVAS)
defined_terms.definition: As defined in the latest series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 138.

defined_terms.label: Accident Emergency Call Systems (AECS)
defined_terms.definition: As defined in the latest series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 144.

applicability_hints: Any electrical and/or electronic device intended to be part of a vehicle that performs a specialized function is an ESA and can be approved under R10 (as component or STU).
Vehicles of all categories L, M, N, O, T, R, S including trailers (O) and agricultural/forestry (T, R, S) are covered; trailers with ABS/EBS or lighting electronics fall in scope.
Aftermarket components not related to immunity related functions need no type approval but require a manufacturer declaration of compliance with paras 6.5–6.9 limits.

Aftermarket or OE components related to immunity related functions (brakes, steering, lighting such as direction indicators/stop lamps/dipped beam, wipers, cameras/indirect vision, airbags, eCall/AECS, horn, alarm, tachograph, odometer, data bus) require approval.
Replacement ESAs identical to and from the same manufacturer as original equipment, marked with an identification number, need no type approval.
LED modules/electronic light sources: an ESA that is (part of) a light source needs an R37/R99/R128 approval number or a non-interchangeability report, otherwise R10 approval is refused.

On-board chargers, charging inlets/control electronics and any ESA in the REESS charging circuit are subject to the additional para 7 requirements (harmonics, flicker, conducted RF, burst, surge, immunity).
Products with signal/control ports (USB, CAN, Control Pilot/PLC) or wired network ports (LAN) used in charging mode may require conducted emission tests on those ports.

Intentional RF transmitters (e.g. radios, telematics units) not approved together with a vehicle manufacturer must be supplied with installation guidelines; vehicle manufacturers must state RF transmitter installation provisions.
ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines are subject to conducted transient immunity and emission tests (Annex 10).
ADS and functions affected in failure situations, AVAS (R138) and AECS (R144) are explicitly referenced and relevant to immunity assessment.
A vehicle with no equipment subject to immunity or emission tests (e.g. a purely mechanical trailer) can obtain R10 approval without testing.
Vehicle type changes in general electrical/electronic component arrangement, wiring arrangement or primary body material create a new vehicle type.
